title: Grade 7 Science — Fri, Jun 20
description: Nutrition in Plants — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review
subject: science

questions.question: Match: Rhizobium → ___
options: Nitrogen-fixing bacterium in legume root nodules
Bacterium that causes disease in plants
questions.explanation: Rhizobium is a nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in the root nodules of leguminous plants. It is an example of mutualism.

questions.question: A plant placed in a completely dark room will eventually die because:
options: It will run out of water
It cannot perform photosynthesis, so no food is produced
questions.explanation: Without light, photosynthesis stops. The plant cannot make glucose, so it starves.

questions.question: Which plant is CORRECTLY matched with its nutrition type?
questions.explanation: Venus flytrap is insectivorous. Cuscuta is parasitic, mushroom is saprotrophic, mango tree is autotrophic.

questions.question: What is the main raw material that enters through stomata for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) enters the leaf through stomata and is used in photosynthesis.

questions.question: The iodine test on a leaf shows no colour change. This means:
options: Photosynthesis has occurred and starch is present
No photosynthesis has occurred (no starch present)
questions.explanation: Iodine turns blue-black in the presence of starch. No colour change means no starch is present, indicating photosynthesis did not occur.

questions.question: Which process returns nitrogen from dead matter back to the soil?
questions.explanation: Saprotrophic bacteria and fungi decompose dead organisms, releasing nitrogen back into the soil as ammonia or nitrates.

questions.question: Which of the following plants can perform photosynthesis AND trap insects?
questions.explanation: Venus flytrap is an insectivorous plant that can still photosynthesize (it has chlorophyll). It traps insects mainly for nitrogen.

questions.question: Where does starch test positive in a variegated leaf?
questions.explanation: Only the green parts of a variegated leaf contain chlorophyll and can photosynthesize, producing starch. White/yellow parts test negative.

questions.question: What do all modes of nutrition (autotrophic, heterotrophic, saprotrophic) have in common?
options: They all result in obtaining nutrients/energy for survival
They all involve eating other organisms
questions.explanation: Despite different methods, all modes of nutrition serve the same purpose — obtaining nutrients and energy for growth and survival.

questions.question: Nitrogen enters the plant in the form of:
questions.explanation: Plants absorb nitrogen as soluble nitrate ions (NO₃⁻) through their roots from the soil.

questions.question: A student claims: 'All bacteria are harmful.' Which example disproves this?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium is a beneficial bacterium that fixes nitrogen and helps leguminous plants grow. Not all bacteria are harmful.

questions.question: By-products of photosynthesis that benefit humans and animals are:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis produces oxygen (which we breathe) and glucose (which feeds the food chain). Both benefit animals and humans.

questions.question: Which organism is a DECOMPOSER that plays a role in the nitrogen cycle?
questions.explanation: Bread mould (Rhizopus) is a saprotrophic decomposer that breaks down dead organic matter, releasing nitrogen back to the soil.

questions.question: Photosynthesis takes place during the day. What process takes place in plants both day AND night?
questions.explanation: Respiration (breaking down glucose for energy) occurs in all cells day and night. Photosynthesis only occurs in light.

questions.question: Which combination correctly completes: Autotroph = ___ ; Heterotroph = ___
questions.explanation: Mango tree is an autotroph (makes its own food via photosynthesis). Lion is a heterotroph (eats other organisms). This is the classic example pair.
